drafts.title: Federal EV road fee ~$130-$135 was eyed for Oct 1. It is on hold for now.
drafts.window: Thursday ~10 AM MT primary; late morning-afternoon OK. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Oct 1, 2026 was the date floated for a new national annual EV registration fee in the House BUILD America 250 draft. USA TODAY (Sep 25): the larger surface-transportation bill stalled, Congress passed a temporary funding extension into December, so EV drivers will not begin paying the proposed national fee on Oct 1. Draft fee about $130/year for EVs (earlier talk of $135), rising by $5/year toward a $150 cap; plug-in hybrids about $35 rising toward $50. Soft politics. Soft lease ladders. Soft Fairfax Equinox inventory LIVE. Kitchen-table: your home cents/kWh still matter more than a delayed registration fee for weekly miles.
bullets: USA TODAY (Sep 25, 2026): proposed national EV fee was tied to a five-year surface transportation bill that has not cleared the full House/Senate; temporary transportation funding continues Highway Trust Fund programs until about Dec. 11.
Draft BUILD America 250 language: EV fee about $130/year starting October (earlier proposal ~$135), +$5/year up to ~$150; plug-in hybrid about $35 rising toward ~$50 by 2031.
Fee would be collected at vehicle registration (no mileage tracker in this draft), aimed at Highway Trust Fund because EVs do not pay the 18.4 cents/gallon federal gas tax.
USA TODAY cites DOE: EV drivers can save about $2,200/year on fuel vs gas; hybrid about $1,500/year - soft-pedal turning into a politics sermon.
Soft-pedal Equinox Fairfax inventory LIVE; soft-pedal Patterson/Vail/Fruita/Gypsum price-only twins.
drafts.body:
Today is October 1.

A national EV registration fee around one hundred thirty dollars a year was on the calendar talk list for today. USA TODAY reported the bill that carried it stalled, and the temporary funding bridge means that fee does not start today.

Soft-pedal the cable-news fight. Soft-pedal party labels. Soft-pedal "EVs freeload" vs "tax the EV."

Here is the kitchen-table sticky note for a 45-year-old shopping a family EV, or a 62-year-old who already bought one:

1) Write YOUR home cents per kilowatt-hour next to a week of pump dollars.
2) Soft-pedal waiting for Washington to make the monthly payment feel better. Home charge is still the independence lever.
3) Soft-pedal panic or celebration. A delayed fee is not the same as "EVs are free forever."
4) Soft-pedal Manheim used-price tickers and lease ladders.
5) If you already drive electric, keep the cheap miles at home and use retail DC for trips.

35-54 line: Premium saves "Oct 1 fee on hold / ~$130 / still do home $/kWh math."

55+ line: independence is knowing your own fuel math when Congress changes the calendar.

drafts.title: Home charge ~$694/year vs DC-fast ~$2,043: Colorado about $0.1654/kWh.
drafts.window: Thursday ~10 AM MT primary; late morning-afternoon OK. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Qmerit 2026 home-vs-public analysis (reviewed Aug 2026): at about $0.18/kWh national average, home charging a typical ~72 kWh pack costs about $13 per fill (~$694/year at 13,489 miles). Public Level 2 about $0.25/kWh (~$964/year). Public DC-fast about $0.53/kWh (~$2,043/year). Colorado residential rate in their EIA-based table about $0.1654/kWh (~$11.91 for 72 kWh). Electric Choice updated Oct 1, 2026: national home full 60 kWh about $11 at ~18.34 cents/kWh; DC-fast about 2-3x. Soft-pedal Patterson/Vail/Fruita/Gypsum price-only twins. Soft-pedal lease ladders. Kitchen-table for first EV at 62 in Grand Junction: home overnight is the independence lever; retail DC is for trips.
bullets: Qmerit: home ~$0.18/kWh -> ~$13 per ~72 kWh charge; ~$694/year at 13,489 miles; exclusive public L2 ~$964; exclusive DC-fast ~$2,043 at ~$0.53/kWh.
Qmerit Colorado row (EIA Monthly April 2026 update in their table): about $0.1654/kWh -> about $11.91 for 72 kWh / about $16.54 for 100 kWh.
Qmerit: about 80% of EV charging is done at home; typical Level 2 install about $1,700 + permit (~$282 average in their data).
Electric Choice (updated Oct 1, 2026): U.S. average about 18.34 cents/kWh; ~$11 for a 60 kWh home fill; home about 3x cheaper than DC-fast (~$33 for 60 kWh at ~55 cents in their example).
Soft-pedal federal 30C charger credit (ended June 30, 2026 per Electric Choice); soft-pedal Manheim used-price tickers.
drafts.body:
People ask me if public charging "kills" the EV math.

Qmerit put numbers on the table for 2026. Home overnight around seven hundred dollars a year for average U.S. miles. Living on DC-fast can push past two thousand. Colorado's residential rate in their table sits under seventeen cents a kilowatt-hour. That is western CO kitchen-table territory.

Soft-pedal shaming apartment renters who cannot charge at home. Soft-pedal "never use Superchargers." Soft-pedal turning every I-70 stop into a price-ticker post.

Here is the sticky note:

1) Write YOUR utility cents/kWh next to what you paid at the last DC stop.
2) Soft-pedal buying an EV without a home or workplace plug plan if weekly miles are high.
3) Soft-pedal Level 2 sticker shock without asking the electrician for a real quote and any utility rebate.
4) Soft-pedal lease ladders and used-price tickers. Compare YOUR driveway math.
5) If you already own an EV: schedule overnight when your rate is cheapest; save retail DC for trips.

35-54 line: Premium saves "~$694 vs ~$2,043 / CO ~16.5 cents / overnight."

55+ line: independence is waking up charged without a gas-station stop.

drafts.title: Model Y shoppers still ask: is a home charger worth it? Owners say that's the whole point.
drafts.window: Thursday ~10 AM MT primary; late morning-afternoon OK. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: The Cool Down (Sep 30, 2026) covers a r/TeslaModelY thread: buyer a couple months from Model Y delivery asks if home charging is worth it when a spouse can charge at work. Owners pile on: one six-year EV owner charged away from home "maybe 25 times" for road trips; another claims "300 miles for $2" on a 3 a.m. rate; others say under ~30 miles/day a mobile 120V cord can be enough. Soft-pedal Patterson/Vail twins. Soft-pedal first-Tesla-at-62 soft LIVE twin as the only angle - use as voice, not rehash. Soft-pedal Fairfax Equinox LIVE. Kitchen-table: home charge is habit + independence, not a luxury accessory.
bullets: Cool Down / Reddit thread (Sep 30, 2026): soon-to-be Model Y owner asks if home charger is worth it when workplace charging exists; many owners say almost all charging is at home.
Six-year EV owner quote in piece: charged away from home maybe 25 times, mostly road trips.
Overnight savings anecdote in piece: "300 miles for $2" at 3 a.m.; rates vary wildly (Toronto 2.8 cents/kWh anecdote vs $0.34/kWh + $25/month meter anecdote).
Owners note: under ~30 miles/day, Level 1 / travel charger can cover commute; public-only can erase EV savings in high-price areas.
Soft-pedal Fairfax Equinox inventory LIVE; soft-pedal lease ladders.
drafts.body:
I bought my first EV at 62.

The question that never dies: "Do I really need a charger at home?"

The Cool Down walked a Model Y buyer thread this week. Owners kept saying the same thing. You go to bed. You wake up around eighty percent. That is the product for weekly life. Public fast charge is the road-trip tool.

Soft-pedal shaming people who only have apartment plugs. Soft-pedal "you must spend two thousand on Level 2 tomorrow." Soft-pedal turning western Colorado Supercharger stops into the only story.

Sticky note:

1) Map YOUR weekly miles. Under about thirty a day, a travel cord can be a start.
2) Ask your utility for any overnight or EV rate before you panic-buy hardware.
3) Soft-pedal workplace-only plans if the job changes.
4) Soft-pedal retail DC as your daily gas station.
5) If you already charge at home: take a phone photo of the cable and say what you actually pay.

35-54 line: Premium saves "home charge = the product / public = trips."

55+ line: independence is not hunting a plug every Tuesday after dinner.

drafts.title: Senate permitting deal: data centers pay for the grid upgrades, not your bill.
drafts.window: Thursday ~10 AM MT primary; late morning-afternoon OK. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: Sep 30, 2026: Sens. Heinrich, Lee, Capito, and Whitehouse introduced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. Senate ENR press: bill "forces data centers to pay their fair share by requiring them to pay for all of their associated transmission costs." Bloomberg/Energy Connects: 417-page deal speeds federal approval of pipelines, power lines, and other projects while requiring data-center developers to pay for high-voltage lines, generation, and distribution rather than passing those costs to consumers; data centers would report energy use to EIA. Vote not until after November midterms. Soft politics. Soft Florida/NJ/Virginia large-load five twins. Soft Revolution Wind / TerraPower twins. Kitchen-table: who pays when AI buildings show up on the grid.
bullets: Senate Energy press Sep 30, 2026: Heinrich (D-NM), Lee (R-UT), Capito (R-WV), Whitehouse (D-RI) introduce Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026.
Press quote principle: data centers pay for associated transmission costs; Heinrich: incremental generation/transmission/distribution "cannot be rate-based and passed on to somebody's electric bill."
Bloomberg via Energy Connects: ~417-page agreement; data centers report energy use to EIA; Senate vote expected after November midterms - not law yet.
Also includes faster federal permitting for infrastructure and a 150-day NEPA lawsuit window after permit issuance (soft-pedal deep politics; keep household who-pays).
Soft-pedal Revolution Wind / TerraPower / Florida SB 484 twins as the same post.
drafts.body:
AI buildings use a lot of electricity.

Families should not be the silent cosigners.

Four senators from both parties put out a permitting bill yesterday that says the quiet part out loud: if a data center needs new generation or new lines, that cost should not land on your residential bill by default.

Soft-pedal party scorekeeping. Soft-pedal "this already passed." It has not. Soft-pedal climate sermons and oil-vs-wind cage matches. The kitchen-table line is who pays.

Sticky note:

1) Ask your utility and public counsel: will large new loads pay for their own upgrades?
2) Soft-pedal celebrating a press release. Watch for a real vote after November.
3) Soft-pedal "AI is free prosperity" and "AI is the villain." Ask for the cost allocation rule.
4) Soft-pedal twinning every state large-load tariff as if they were identical.
5) If you already watch your bill: write this month's cents/kWh on a sticky note and keep the receipt trail.

35-54 line: Premium saves "data centers pay transmission / not ratepayers / not law yet."

55+ line: independence is not subsidizing somebody else's server hall by accident.

drafts.title: AI scams got cheap: family code word + hang-up-and-call-back beat deepfakes.
drafts.window: Thursday ~10 AM MT primary; late morning-afternoon OK. Soft-pedal 8am primary.
drafts.angle: AARP (detecting AI fraud): criminals use cheap AI for deepfake videos, cloned voices, and impostor chats; Microsoft analysis of AARP/BBB data found AI-identified scams up about 20-fold from 2023 to 2025; nearly 9 in 10 older adults worry about AI-enabled scams (U-M National Poll on Healthy Aging cited); voice clone can need only seconds of audio; half of AARP Helpline scams in 2025 were impostor schemes. Practical defenses: slow down, hang up and call the number on your statement, family safe word, never pay with gift cards or crypto kiosks, report to IC3.gov / AARP Helpline 877-908-3360. Soft-pedal MyChart LIVE twin (this is family code-word / voice-clone, not Medicare kit phishing). Soft-pedal overnight AI-appointments soft LIVE twin. Kitchen-table money/independence for 55+.
bullets: AARP: AI-enabled scams include deepfake video, cloned voice, impostor sites/emails/texts; FBI warns surge; Microsoft study with AARP/BBB data: AI-identified scams increased about 20-fold 2023 to 2025.
Nearly 9 in 10 older adults worried about AI-enabled scams (AARP cites 2025 University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging).
Voice cloning: experts cited saying a photo plus about three seconds of voice can be enough for a deepfake with audio (was hours of audio years ago).
Half of scams reported to AARP Helpline in 2025 were impostor schemes (mostly business/government, not family impersonation).

Defenses AARP lists: pause; do not trust caller ID; hang up and call official number; family safe word; never gift cards/crypto kiosks for "official" payments; report IC3.gov; AARP Fraud Watch Helpline 877-908-3360.
drafts.body:
This is not a MyChart email warning. Different scam shape.

AI made fake voices and fake videos cheap. AARP walked the new playbook. Older households are worried for a reason. Impostors pretend to be the bank, a government office, or a job offer. Grammar mistakes are no longer the tell.

Soft-pedal fear-mongering. Soft-pedal "throw away the smartphone." Soft-pedal twinning yesterday's Medicare Kit post. Soft-pedal AI-appointments LIVE as a twin.

Sticky note for your kitchen table:

1) Pick a family code word. If "grandson" calls in a panic and does not know it, hang up.
2) Hang up. Call the number on your bank statement or on the real agency site. Never the number the caller gives you.
3) Soft-pedal urgency. Real banks do not make you buy gift cards or walk cash to a Bitcoin machine.
4) Soft-pedal clicking links in surprise texts.
5) If something feels wrong, call AARP's fraud helpline or report at IC3.gov - and tell one trusted person the same day.

35-54 line: Premium saves "code word / hang up / AI impostor / not MyChart twin."

55+ line: independence is keeping your savings when a fake voice sounds perfect.
